source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 6 June 1952, p. 5 ("County and rural council elections: results"); Irish News, 21 May 1952, p. 7 ("Nominations for the local elections"); Mid-Ulster Mail, 14 June 1952, p. 6 ("Rural Council Elections")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)

note: Triennial election of the 16 electoral divisions of Cookstown rural district, one member each, polled on 5 June 1952. Seventeen candidates were nominated (nine Unionists, six Nationalists, two Independents); Beaghmore and Lissan were contested and the other thirteen nominees were returned unopposed (Mid-Ulster Mail, 24 May 1952, p. 5). No nomination was received for Killycolpy; the paper expected the retiring member, Mr. Patrick J. Duffy, senr., to be re-elected; as the retiring member he was deemed re-elected. Labels are the list's group headings. Miss Loughran is the first woman elected to the council.
